clue.text: After a time, disorder is contained by country's leader … needing this?

definitions.text: After a time, disorder is contained by country's leader … needing this?

indicators.note: being contained by something means sitting inside it, so the leader's letters wrap round the rest

parts.note: PM, the Prime Minister, leads the country

indicators.note: the word for disorder follows the letters for a time, so it comes after them

parts.note: a riot is public disorder
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nation in turmoil, its premier keeping order, calls for love of country.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: the wordplay builds the answer and the clue as a whole hints at what a troubled country's leader would want from citizens.
explanation.definitionFit: Love of one's country is what a leader facing unrest would need from the people.

clue.text: Northerner selected for speech

indicators.note: for speech means the word is to be spoken rather than read, signalling a sound-alike

parts.note: selected means picked

explanation.surface: Someone from the north was chosen to give an address.
explanation.definitionFit: The Picts were an ancient people of northern Scotland, so a member of that people is a northerner.

clue.text: Climbing fan finds peak of Everest a strain

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means going upwards, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: a nut is an enthusiast or fan

indicators.note: the peak of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An eager mountaineer finds the summit of Everest an effort.
explanation.definitionFit: A strain is a melody or snatch of music, a synonym for an air.

clue.text: Art exhibit in local office enthralling everyone

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so one word holds another inside it

parts.note: a station, such as a local police station, is a local office
everyone means all

explanation.surface: A gallery piece is on show in a community office that captivates all visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: In modern art an installation is a large exhibit assembled in a gallery space.

clue.text: Religious pamphlet that covers a lot of ground?

definitions.meaning: a short leaflet putting a religious message

definitions.text: that covers a lot of ground?
definitions.meaning: an expanse of land covers a wide area

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a short religious leaflet and a large expanse of land.

clue.text: Flower right for planting in pots, once developed

indicators.note: planting something in a container puts it inside, so one piece is set within the other
developed means worked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener plants a flower in pots that were once overgrown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges the eight fodder letters to STONECOP; 'for planting in' then sets the R for right inside it, before the last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Stonecrop is a sedum, a low succulent plant that bears small starry flowers.

clue.text: Flight formation adopted by various sea birds

indicators.note: something adopted by another is taken into it, so one piece goes inside
various means differing in arrangement, so the letters are shuffled

parts.note: geese flying in a V shape make a flight formation

explanation.surface: Seabirds of different kinds take up a V-shaped formation in flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' rearranges SEA to AES, and 'adopted by' puts V inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Aves is the scientific class name covering all birds.

clue.text: Large house with fifty instruments: no room for English composer

parts.note: a villa is a large house
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

indicators.note: having no room for something leaves it out, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: oboes are woodwind instruments

explanation.surface: A mansion full of woodwind instruments leaves an English composer no space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no room for English' drops E from OBOES, leaving OBOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Heitor Villa-Lobos was a Brazilian composer, best known for the Bachianas Brasileiras.

clue.text: Competent group of workers? That G makes a change, so to speak

definitions.text: That G makes a change, so to speak

parts.note: sound means reliable or competent
a shift is a team of workers on duty together

explanation.surface: A capable team of workers wonders whether the letter G has altered.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to linguistics: a change in how a consonant such as G is pronounced over the history of a language, as in Grimm's law.
explanation.definitionFit: In phonetics a regular change in pronunciation across a language is termed a shift in its spoken form.

clue.text: Grabbed by prison officer, one's seeing stars

indicators.note: something grabbed by another is held within it, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: can is slang for prison
a major is an army officer
one is I, and the 's stands for is, giving I plus S

explanation.surface: A captured prisoner, held by an officer, is dazed and seeing stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is read as I plus the 's of 'one is'; 'Grabbed by' splits the prison-officer pair so that pair goes in the gap between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Canis Major, the Great Dog, is a constellation of stars including Sirius.

clue.text: Main attraction, a hit mostly

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a clout is a blow or hit

explanation.surface: The headline act is mostly a smash success.
explanation.definitionFit: Clou, borrowed from French, is the chief point of interest or star turn.

clue.text: They made way, as horses carried in holy cardinal

indicators.note: the horses carry other letters inside them

parts.note: cobs are sturdy horses
blest means holy or blessed
one is a cardinal number

explanation.surface: A procession makes way as horses carry a saintly cardinal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cardinal' is not a churchman but a cardinal number.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobbles laid side by side formed old road surfaces, so they made the way.

clue.text: Cold water has splashed about country manor

indicators.note: splashed about suggests things thrown around, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Freezing water has been sprayed round a stately home.
explanation.walkthrough: CASTLE HOWARD is a grand stately home in North Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Castle Howard is an English country house, a stately manor rather than a fortress.

clue.text: Solitary little nipper?

parts.note: seems to be a lonely child, but describes a small pincered creature that lives alone in a borrowed shell

explanation.definitionFit: This crustacean has nipping claws and lives alone in a discarded shell, like a recluse.

clue.text: Leaving scene of fight following nasty minute, scrape

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Leaving scene of fight following nasty minute, scrape', parses as RING after an anagram of SCRAPE, but 'minute' has no job; the scan is blank and searches did not find the printed clue
annotationWithheld.clue: Leaving scene of fight following nasty minute, scrape

clue.text: Former measure of ammunition, say, for weapon

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: calibre is the measure of a bullet or gun bore

explanation.surface: An old gauge of ammunition stands in for a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Excalibur is King Arthur's legendary sword, a weapon of myth.

clue.text: Wager Irish Republic will shelter no undesirable

parts.note: a bet is a wager

indicators.note: sheltering something keeps it inside, so one piece goes within

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for the Republic of Ireland
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bettor reckons Ireland will give refuge to no unwanted person.
explanation.definitionFit: A bête noire, French for black beast, is a person or thing one particularly detests.

clue.text: Army leader's stall

definitions.meaning: William ... founded and led the Salvation Army
a small enclosed stand at a market or fair

explanation.definitionFit: The word is the surname of the Salvation Army's founder and also a market stand or kiosk.

clue.text: Revolutionary leader hauled back American deserter

indicators.note: hauled back means pulled the other way, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: a rat is one who deserts a cause

explanation.surface: A rebel chief dragged a turncoat American back.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Paul Marat was a radical leader of the French Revolution, murdered in his bath.

clue.text: Secretly informed of payment gentleman's to announce

indicators.note: announcing is saying aloud, so the letters come from how the words sound

parts.note: a tip is a small payment and a toff is a gentleman, giving TIP then TOFF; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: Someone discreetly tipped off about a gentleman's payment wants to go public.
explanation.definitionFit: To be given a confidential warning or piece of information in advance.

clue.text: Current cost of speed?

definitions.meaning: the usual price prevailing at the moment
a playful reading: the pace at which something goes

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the usual present price, and literally the rate of travel or pace.

clue.text: Estate producing regular supply of Armagnac — ah!

indicators.note: a regular supply takes letters at even intervals, here every second one

explanation.surface: A country property produces a steady flow of brandy, to everyone's delight.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranch is a large farming estate, especially for cattle in North America.

clue.text: Having got up, departed along with others

indicators.note: in a down clue getting up means rising, so the word is read upwards

parts.note: late means dead or departed

explanation.surface: Once they had risen, they set off together with the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin abbreviation meaning and others, used to cut a list of names short.

clue.text: College half-term about end of month

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word means its first two letters

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A college's half-term falls around the close of the month.
explanation.definitionFit: A tech is informal British shorthand for a technical college.

clue.text: Game in a state of collapse

parts.note: RU is Rugby Union, a game
taken as written

explanation.surface: A match is played in a crumbling condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruin is the condition of having fallen into decay or collapse.

clue.text: One blooming war plane heads group of nine (almost ten)

indicators.note: the plane heads the group, so its letters come first

parts.note: a MiG is a Russian fighter plane
a nonet is a group of nine musicians

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter goes

explanation.surface: A fighter plane leads a band of nine, nearly ten, in bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Mignonette is a fragrant garden plant, so it is one that blooms.

clue.text: Items of clothing in luggage

definitions.meaning: old British slang for loose trousers
cases and holdalls carried when travelling

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both baggy trousers in British slang and travelling cases.

clue.text: Hard getting employment in struggling hamlet for old man

indicators.note: one group of letters goes inside the other
struggling suggests disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
use means employment

explanation.surface: Someone tough finds work in a village that is having a hard time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' rearranges the fodder to METLAH, and 'in' sets the H and the word for employment inside it, straight after the T.
explanation.definitionFit: Methuselah, said in Genesis to have lived 969 years, stands for any very old man.
